To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the selective vulnerability of neurons during reperfusion following global cerebral ischemia may be related to their differential susceptibility to lipid peroxidation, which occurs in the cytoplasmic matrix of neurons in the selectively susceptible zones of the cortex (layers 5 and 7) and hippocampus (CA1).

the fluorescent histochemical localization of products of lipid per-oxidation in the selectively vulnerable areas of the brain during reperfusion after cardiac arrest is consistent with the hypothesis that lipid peroxidation is an important mechanism of brain damage during post-ischemia reperfusion.

neurons in the pyramideal layers of the cortex and in the pyrimidal layer of the hippocampus, but not other neurons, are early and specific target cells of lipid peroxidative damage during brain reperfusin following cardiac arrest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the biochemical and cellular mechanisms of brain damage following cardiac arrest and resusciation.
the role of oxygen free radicals and lipid peroxidation in the pathogenesis of ischemic brain injury.
the role of lipid peroxidative processes in brain damage following ischemia and reperfusion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first study to demonstrate that the fluorescent TBA reaction can be used to localize in situ products of lipid peroxide formation during brain reperfection following cardiac arrest.
the fluorescent histochemical method described in the paper is a useful tool for the study of lipid peroxidative processes during brain reperoxidation following cardiac arrest.

the results of this investigation indicate that lipid peroxidation occurs during post-ischemia reperfusion and that this is a major factor contributing to the neuronal death that occurs after ischemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain is very vulnerable to lipid peroxidation following ischemia and that this process is most pronounced in the vulnerable neurons of the cortex and the hippocampus.
the selective vulnerability of neurons during ischemia/reperfusion is due to a selective vulnerability of mitochondria.
lipid peroxidation is an early and selective event in the reperfusion injury of the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is very susceptible to free radical injury, and this injury can be prevented with free radical scavengers.

the TBA reaction can be driven in situ to form fluorescent adducts with lipid peroxidation products, that these adducts can be localized to the neuronal perikaryon in a selective manner, and that the TBA fluorescence can be used to identify selectively vulnerable neurons in the post-ischemic brain.
lipid peroxidation is not a random phenomenon in the brain following cardiac arrest and that the neurons that undergo this process are the ones that are selectively vulnerable to ischemic injury.
